quote: I do want to just double check with my manager and make sure we are able to help.
stewart_read: This is not a documented Ion protocol in the schema (tenant-billing on a multi-unit rental isn't in dq_rules or protocols), so the rep is applying an ungoverned, improvised check. The vague justification ('sometimes it happens like that') is what triggered the customer's irritation, not the check itself.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep simply didn't have a clean explanation ready and fumbled it live. Strategic read (rejected): there's no evidence the hold was a deliberate stall tactic — it reads as genuine uncertainty about a real edge case (multi-unit landlord/tenant metering).
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to have a one-line, confident explanation ready for multi-unit/tenant-metering scenarios before going to hold, so the customer doesn't hear 'I don't know' as the justification for making them wait.

quote: Yeah. Right. I'm just a a scheduler, so I don't really know a bunch of the specifics. Right?
stewart_read: Rep correctly names her own scope limit here after already having partially engaged on ownership-vs-lease details a few lines earlier — this is the right instinct arriving a beat late.

coaching_implication: Reinforce the 'I'm just a scheduler' framing as the FIRST response to ownership/pricing mechanics, not the fallback after already speculating on options.

quote: Yeah. So our panels are manufactured in Washington. They're from Silfab, rep: and we use in phase microinverters.
stewart_read: Customer asked a product-spec question mid-tangent and the rep answered with real manufacturing/equipment detail instead of redirecting — textbook scope creep even though the customer seemed genuinely curious rather than objecting.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read (accepted): there's no strategic payoff visible here; the rep simply answered the question because she knew it, rather than bridging to the specialist.
coaching_implication: Flag as a habit to interrupt: even friendly, curious customer questions about specs should route to 'that's exactly what the specialist covers' to protect appointment value.
